events.summary: Programmed (rotating) power cuts were carried out in Kuwait on 9 April 2025, reaching parts of some residential, agricultural and industrial areas, when electrical load ran well above the same day a year earlier. The electricity ministry later said the load rise of 9 and 10 April 2025 required a programme of programmed cuts.
events.effect: The electricity ministry stated on 13 April 2025 that loads on 9 and 10 April 2025 were about 21% and 17.3% above the same period of the previous year, 'which required implementing a programme of programmed cuts'. The press reported that on 9 April the ministry cut power to parts of some residential, agricultural and industrial areas, eight residential areas being named, under what the ministry called an emergency plan for peak loads.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4, second limb (a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages): the ministry's own page says the load rise of 9-10 April 2025 'required implementing a programme of programmed cuts', and a newspaper names eight residential areas cut on 9 April. Neither source uses the words generation shortfall, and no megawatts-shed figure is given.

events.summary: Programmed (rotating) power cuts of one to two hours were applied to parts of about 40 areas across Kuwait's six governorates on 19 June 2024, when generation could not meet peak demand in extreme heat; on 20 June the ministry published a list of areas that might be cut and cuts were reported in a few agricultural and industrial areas.
events.effect: The electricity ministry stated on 19 June 2024 that the cuts in parts of the six governorates were due to 'the inability of the power generating plants to meet the rising demand during the peak period', applied as programmed cuts of one to two hours at most. The press counted about 40 areas and reported a 300 MW generating unit out of service that day.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4, second limb (a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages): the ministry's own statement gives the cause as plants unable to meet peak demand and describes programmed cuts of one to two hours; about 40 areas were affected on a dated day.

events.summary: A fuel supply shortfall on 17 August 2024, which the electricity ministry described as a fault in fuel (gas) supplies, reduced generation in Kuwait, and the ministry cut power to parts of a number of residential areas on 18 August 2024; programmed cuts in agricultural and industrial areas were still being applied on 19 August.
events.effect: The electricity ministry, in a statement carried by the state news agency on 18 August 2024, attributed the cuts to 'a fault in fuel (gas) supplies' that took generating units out of service, and said the cuts were made to keep the grid stable. On 19 August the ministry said cuts in nine agricultural and industrial areas were applied in turn because of the gas supply problem.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4 (a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages): generating units went out after a fuel supply fault and the ministry cut residential areas, then agricultural and industrial areas one after another, on dated days. No megawatt figure is given.

events.summary: Programmed power cuts returned in Kuwait on 10 September 2024: the electricity ministry cut power to parts of 11 residential areas, and to some non-residential areas, after two generating units went out of service unexpectedly while load was near its record.
events.effect: The electricity ministry announced on 10 September 2024 that it was cutting power to parts of 11 residential areas; the press reported an emergency outage of two generating units, 390 MW together according to an unnamed ministry source.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4, second limb (a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages): two units lost unexpectedly and programmed cuts applied to parts of 11 residential areas on a dated day.

events.summary: An attack was reported on a refinery in Kuwait on 20 March 2026.
events.effect: An official statement said a fire broke out in some of the refinery's units and that a number of units were shut.
